# create-preview

You are handed an **Intent** (or a feature request that becomes one). Before the real implementation you build a
**Preview** (a Mock or a Draft), let the human give feedback on it in the qy recorder, iterate, and turn the agreed
result into **acceptance criteria (AC)** the human locks. After the real implementation, the human records an
acceptance run on the real app, and that run is promoted into a regression suite. Invoke as
`/create-preview <intent-id | request>`.

The rules of the Intent Align protocol (layout, id, file formats, human gates) are in the `intent-protocol` skill.
Load it if it is not already loaded. Paths below starting with `intent/` mean `.qarify/intents/{id}/`.

Reply to the user in the user's own language. The exact wording of the confirmation messages below is a
template, not a script.

## 0. Preflight

- Check whether the qy MCP tools are available (`qy_preview_open`, `qy_feedback_get`, `qy_feedback_status`,
  `qy_spec_promote`, `qy_spec_run`).
  - **Available** -> follow the _Agent path_ (section 5) end to end.
  - **Not available** -> tell the user to open the qy UI **Preview** page (`Manual path`): the user records and
    reviews there and gives you the feedback with the page's **Copy as Markdown** button. You still do every
    step of sections 0.5-8 that writes intent files (feedback snapshot from the pasted markdown, Decisions, AC
    draft, gates); only the tool calls in section 5 are replaced by the user's actions.
- Never invent tool names, feedback ids or file contents.

## 0.5 Bind the Intent

- **Named intent** -> read `intent/intent.md` (body + frontmatter) and any answered Decisions in `intent/decisions.md`.
- **Plain request** -> propose a new intent id `{YYMMDD}-{slug}` and a `title`; after the user confirms, create
  `intent/intent.md` with the request verbatim as the body (`intent-protocol` §1.1, §2).
- **Not sure which intent** -> list `.qarify/intents/` and ask. Never guess.
- `intent.md` says `preview: skip` -> tell the user and stop unless they override.
- The qy `<feature>` name is the **intent id** (`{id}-{part}` if the intent needs several Previews).
- Set `stage: align` in `intent.md` frontmatter when the first Preview opens, and register the Preview in
  `previews:` (`{feature, kind, feedbackIds}`); append each new `feedbackId`.

## 1. Step 0 - Mock or Draft (mandatory, user-confirmed)

### Mock / Draft decision checklist

Apply this to EVERY feature request, mechanically, before writing any Preview. Do not guess an answer you cannot
derive from the request: ask the user a short clarifying question first.

**Gating question (ask first).** Can a Draft actually be implemented at Preview time? If external dependencies
make even a minimal vertical slice impossible (no real OAuth provider credentials, no payment gateway, ...),
the answer is **No**: choose **Mock** regardless of the score, and tell the user that the server-side parts a
Mock cannot show should be captured as comments.

**Five scored questions (Yes/No each):**

| # | Question | Yes means |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Is the screen layout / interaction flow (new screen, form, navigation, information layout) the CORE of judging whether the requirement is met? | Mock +1 |
| Q2 | Is it impossible to judge the requirement without server logic (business rules, auth, DB transaction)? | Draft +1 |
| Q3 | Are runtime async state changes (loading -> done, progress, polling, live update, retry) the core of the requirement? | Draft +1 |
| Q4 | Must existing codebase components/modules be reused AS-IS for the check to be meaningful (replacing them would distort the result)? | Draft +1 |
| Q5 | Do the success/failure/response DATA of server API calls decide the screen's behaviour branches? | Draft +1 |

**Decision rule.** `M = 1` if Q1 is Yes, else `0`. `D` = number of Yes answers among Q2..Q5 (0..4).
**Draft if and only if `D > M`; otherwise (including ties) Mock.** In practice: Q1 = No -> Draft from `D >= 1`;
Q1 = Yes -> Draft from `D >= 2`. When unsure or under time pressure, start with the cheaper option (Mock) and
state that assumption explicitly.

**Always ask the user to confirm.** Post the decision plus the scoring rationale (which questions were Yes/No,
the values of `M` and `D`, whether the gating question was triggered) and WAIT for an explicit OK before you
write anything. The confirmation is mandatory and can never be skipped.

**Intent hints.** An intent whose feature lives inside an existing app shell (auth, routing, layout) leans Draft;
a greenfield screen leans Mock. These are hints for answering Q1..Q5, not overrides of the rule.

Known limits: the gating question depends on your own knowledge of what can be wired up at Preview time; and
non-functional requirements (performance, security, accessibility) do not fit Q1..Q5 - record them as comments or
Decisions.

Confirmation message template (adapt the language):

> "This feature is <reason: which questions were Yes/No; M=<m>, D=<d>; gating: <passed|triggered>>, so I plan to
> build a <Mock|Draft>. Shall I proceed?"

Do not create any file before the user confirms. If you had to assume an unknown answer, say so here.

## 2. Mock rules (when the decision is Mock)

- One directory per feature under `.qarify/mocks/`, one sub-directory per screen:
  `.qarify/mocks/<feature>/<screen>/index.html` (+ `mock.json`). `<feature>` MUST match
  `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` (lower-case kebab/snake; no dots, no slashes).
- Mock data lives in `.qarify/mocks/<feature>/<screen>/mock.json`.
- Feature metadata lives in `.qarify/mocks/<feature>/meta.json`:
  `{"kind":"mock","title":"...","description":"...","entry":"<optional relative path, default: index/index.html or the first screen>"}`
  and describes the directory structure and each directory's role (shown in the qy UI list).
  **Do NOT put a start URL in meta**: qy serves `.qarify/mocks` itself and issues the URL.
- Implement with plain HTML, CSS (Tailwind CSS) and JavaScript.
- **Use relative URLs only** (`./app.js`, `../shared/style.css`). qy serves a Mock under a project-scoped prefix
  (`/mocks/<projectId>/<feature>/...`), so absolute paths such as `/assets/x.js` break.
- Prefer no external CDN so the Mock also works offline / on an intranet. If you do use a CDN (e.g. Tailwind), say
  so in `meta.description`.
- Follow the `data-testid` rule (section 4).

## 3. Draft rules (when the decision is Draft)

- Write the code **in place**, where the real implementation will live. Do not create a parallel mock codebase.
- Feature metadata lives in `.qarify/drafts/<feature>/meta.json`:
  `{"kind":"draft","title":"...","startUrl":"http://localhost:<port>/<path>","policyTodos":[...]}`.
- Cover ONE happy path only.
- Every point that needs a policy decision (concurrent runs allowed? cancellable? failure handling? retry policy?)
  is implemented with the **simplest arbitrary default** and marked in code:
  `// POLICY-TODO[<id>]: <description>` where `<id>` is a stable kebab-case id. Register each marker as
  `{ "id", "description", "file", "line" }` through `qy_preview_open`'s `policyTodos` argument or in `meta.json`.
- Every `POLICY-TODO[<id>]` also becomes a Decision `D-n` in `intent/decisions.md` (`Affects: POLICY-TODO[<id>]`)
  so the human can answer it as text instead of recording it.
- No UI polish, no accessibility work, no performance work.
- A Draft is **not disposable**: the real implementation extends it. Remove a `POLICY-TODO` marker once resolved
  and update `policyTodos` accordingly.
- You (or the user) start the dev server; qy does not manage it. If `qy_preview_open` fails with
  `preview-unreachable`, start the dev server and retry.
- The scenario must be re-runnable (account seeding/reset is the project's responsibility).
- **Repeat cap = 2.** If `POLICY-TODO` items are still unresolved after 2 record -> review loops, tell the user
  explicitly and ask them to answer the matching Decisions; do not keep looping.
- A Mock has **no** numeric cap. If a Mock loop grows abnormally long, re-apply the checklist (section 1) and
  reconsider Draft.

## 4. `data-testid` rule (Mock and Draft)

1. Every NEW or MODIFIED interactive or asserted element MUST carry `data-testid="<feature>-<element>"`
   (kebab-case, stable, unique on the page).
2. For EXISTING elements that the recorded happy path clicks, types into or asserts, you MUST add a `data-testid`
   when one is absent - a one-attribute, behaviour-neutral edit.
3. Do NOT add test ids to elements the flow does not touch (no codebase-wide sweep).
4. Mock/Draft -> real implementation: keep the same ids (tests and the acceptance recording rely on them).

## 5. Alignment loop (Agent path, qy MCP tools)

The tools never block on the human: they start something and return. Never poll.

1. Ask "Shall I open the preview now?". Only after the user says yes call
   `qy_preview_open({action:"record", feature, kind, startUrl?, policyTodos?})`. For a Draft pass `startUrl` (and
   `policyTodos`); for a Mock pass only `feature` and `kind:"mock"`. Keep the returned `feedbackId` and register it
   in `intent.md` `previews`.
2. Tell the user to record their feedback in the browser (with comments) and to say when they are done.
   Do nothing until the user says so.
3. Call `qy_feedback_get({feedbackId, view:"full"})` for the first read, and `view:"actionable"` after every
   re-review. **Save the returned markdown verbatim to `intent/feedback/{feedbackId}/feedback.md`.** Apply the
   requested changes (Mock/Draft files), following sections 2-4. A comment that is really a policy question
   (a limit, a rule, a permission) becomes a Decision in `intent/decisions.md` instead of a guess in the Preview.
4. Ask "Shall I open the review now?", then call
   `qy_preview_open({action:"review", feedbackId})`. If you omit `feedbackId` and the tool answers
   `ambiguous-feedback`, choose from the candidates it lists - never guess.
5. After the user says the review is done, call `qy_feedback_status({feature})`. If any comment is still
   `pending`/`rejected` (or `playbackFailures > 0`), go back to step 3 with `view:"actionable"`.
6. **AC draft.** When the feedback is `approved`, write or update `intent/spec/acceptance.md` (`locked: false`):
   one AC per approved comment (including comments with no assertion), per answered Decision that changes
   behavior, and per explicit check in the intent (`intent-protocol` §5, `Source` mandatory). Set
   `stage: baseline`.
7. **Baseline gate (human).** Show the user the open Decisions and the AC list and ask them to answer / edit and
   say _lock_. Only after an explicit OK set `locked: true`, `lockedAt`, `lockedBy: human (transcribed)`.
   Never lock on your own judgment. Then set `stage: build`.
8. Implement the real feature (Draft: extend the Draft code and resolve each `POLICY-TODO[id]` per its answered
   Decision; Mock: build the real app). Keep every `data-testid`.
9. **Acceptance recording (human).** When the real implementation runs, ask "Shall I open the acceptance
   recording on the real app?", then call
   `qy_preview_open({action:"record", feature, kind:"draft", startUrl:"<real app URL>"})` and give the user the
   locked AC ids and texts as a checklist: for each AC they perform the flow and add an assertion/comment at the
   point that proves it. Save the snapshot (step 3), run the review loop (steps 4-5) on this feedback, and set
   `stage: verify`.
10. When this acceptance feedback is `approved` (`promotable: true`), ask permission and call
    `qy_spec_promote({feedbackId})`. Read `confirmationRun` and `selectorAdvisories` in the result. Fill
    `Verified by` in `acceptance.md` for each AC the promoted suite covers; list AC it does not cover.
11. Call `qy_spec_run({suiteKey})` until it is green; use the reported failed steps to fix the code. Add the
    suite key to `intent.md` `affectedSuites`.
12. **Sign-off (human).** Set `stage: signoff` and report per AC: covered by which test, pass/fail, gaps. The
    user signs off; then set `stage: done`, `status: done`.

**Mock feedback is never promoted** (`qy_spec_promote` is only called on an acceptance recording on the real app,
or on a Draft feedback after the baseline lock when the user asks for it). A Mock feedback ends at `approved`; its
value is the AC it produced.

A `promoted` feedback is **read-only**. Any further change is a NEW `qy_preview_open({action:"record"})`.
`commentCount: 0` on an approved feedback means the user recorded no comments - point that out.

## 6. Ports and URLs

- Mock URLs embed the qy server port. Pin it with `QY_REVIEW_PORT` to keep recorded origins stable across
  restarts.
- The acceptance recording uses the real app URL; Mock URLs never end up in a promoted suite.

## 7. Never

- Never skip a user-confirmation step (Mock/Draft decision, "open the preview?", "open the review?", "lock?",
  "open the acceptance recording?", "promote?").
- Never answer a Decision, lock AC or sign off on the user's behalf.
- Never promote a Mock feedback.
- Never rename an intent directory.
- Never fabricate a `feedbackId`.
- Never edit `feedback-*.json` files by hand.
- Never start or stop the recorder except through the tools.

## 8. Conversation rules

Every "shall I proceed?" question is YOUR job, not a tool's. Keep each confirmation short and specific.
When you stop at a human gate, say exactly what the user must do, with file paths and ids (D-n, AC-n).
